# Lexicon

> Speech-to-text gets English right and your names wrong. Lexicon is one YAML file of the words a person actually says. It rewrites the transcript before an agent reads it. It is not a dictation app.

Agents are first-class users. Do not install it unasked. Preview, show the plan, then apply.

Install (Node 20+). The script runs `lexicon setup` when it has a terminal. Without a terminal, under `sudo`, or with `LEXICON_NO_SETUP=1`, it only installs and ends with `run: lexicon setup`.

```bash
curl -fsSL https://ashlrai.github.io/lexicon/install.sh | sh
```

No global install:

```bash
npx @ashlr/lexicon@latest setup
```

Preview, write nothing:

```bash
lexicon setup --dry-run --json
```

Correct a transcript. Stdout is one JSON document. Read `ok`, then `output`. `example: true` means the built-in sample stood in and nothing was written.

```bash
lexicon normalize "ask ashler to deploy kuber netties with post gressql" --json
```

MCP server. Preview (`applied` is false), then write:

```bash
lexicon install claude --json
lexicon install claude --apply --json
lexicon install cursor --json
lexicon install cursor --apply --json
lexicon install codex --json
lexicon install codex --apply --json
```

Hand config, only when `lexicon-mcp` is on PATH.

Claude Code and Cursor (`~/.cursor/mcp.json`):

    {
      "mcpServers": {
        "lexicon": { "command": "lexicon-mcp", "args": [] }
      }
    }

Codex (`~/.codex/config.toml`):

    [mcp_servers.lexicon]
    command = "lexicon-mcp"
    args = []
